summary: A 1935 CCC-built C-3 cab on a 17-ft tower in Tahoe National Forest, replacing a 1915 original, refurbished 2009 and now a rentable observation cab near Sierraville, CA.

facts.design: 14'x14' C-3 cab on an enclosed 17-ft wood tower, built by the CCC

access.note: Reached via dirt/gravel Forest Service roads off Hwy 89; last quarter mile is a walk-in past a locked gate.

visit.trail_note: Iron gate forces parking and a quarter-mile walk to the tower.

events.note: First structure was a 4-A cab on an enclosed wood tower
Current 14'x14' C-3 cab on a 17-ft enclosed tower built by the CCC on the Tahoe National Forest
Refurbished and made available for public rental

evidence.quote: The first structure at Sardine Point Lookout was 4-A cab on an enclosed wood tower built in 1915.
The current 14'x14' C-3 cab on an enclosed 17' tower was constructed in 1935 by the CCC on the Tahoe National Forest.
Sardine Peak is a forest fire lookout tower that was constructed in 1935 by the Civilian Conservation Corps. It is a three story enclosed tower with external stairs.
Sardine Peak with refurbished in 2009 and is available for public rental.

evidence.supports: not currently staffed; Babbitt Peak staffed instead
evidence.quote:
Staffed?
No
Babbitt Peak, 6 miles to the north east is staffed
An Iron gate will force you to park and walk the last quarter mile.

evidence.supports: no electricity, water, or garbage service; propane appliances
evidence.quote: The lookout does not have electricity, water or garbage service. It does have a propane tank to operate propane-powered appliances.

evidence.supports: interior furnishings of the rentable cab
evidence.quote: The interior of the cab is 14 feet long and 14 feet wide and contains two twin beds, a dry sink, a table and four chairs, two propane lights, a propane cast iron heat stove and a propane stove/oven for cooking.

evidence.supports: call ranger district before arrival for conditions
evidence.quote: Before arrival, visitors should call the Sierraville Ranger District at (530) 430-8912 (Monday through Friday) for road, weather and fire conditions between 8:30AM and 12:30 PM.

evidence.supports: elevation ~8,100 ft; views of Sierra Buttes, Sierra Valley, Truckee; dirt/gravel road easily traveled by low-clearance 2WD
evidence.quote: Elevation 8,135 ft (2,480 m) ... It’s all dirt/gravel road. Most of it very good, some of it a bit rough, but nonetheless easily traveled by 2 wheel drive low clearance vehicles. An Iron gate will force you to park and walk the last quarter mile. Views are awesome. You’ll see the Sierra Buttes, Sierra Valley to the North/West; Truckee to the North.

sources.title: Sardine Peak Lookout Tower, Tahoe National Forest

notes_for_editor: No source found detailing what fires Sardine Peak watched for or who staffed it historically beyond the current unstaffed status. Height_m in the brief (2479.5, an elevation not structure height) was left unchanged since no source gave a differing figure (nhlr.org lists elevation as 8,135 ft / 2,480 m).
